text:
Mia: quick heads-up — I ran a small rogue-prefetch sketch on the 13B draft model this morning, wanted to surface numbers and hear thoughts.
Devin: nice, summary please.
Mia: tl;dr: ~1.9x median token throughput, ~22% fewer model calls (KV hits), but a small quality dip on our conv-bench (win-rate vs baseline down ~0.6%).
Samir: can you paste the exact config? guessing prefetch window + early-fallthrough?
Mia: yep — two-tier prefetch: short-window speculative fetch (k=4), fallback to normal path if entropy>threshold. Implementation: lightweight sampler that primes KV cache for likely next tokens.
Olivia: interesting. how did you measure "win-rate"?
Mia: paired A/B on 5k stratified prompts (mix of code, dialog, instructions). Win-rate is fraction of prompts where candidate from baseline beats speculative output per human EVAL rubric. We used MBR + pairwise preference for ties.
Devin: any automated metrics correlate? pplx/perplexity? rouge?
Mia: perplexity dropped slightly (better) because prefetch reduces autoreg noise when correct; but BLEU/ROUGE stable. The manual pairwise preference captured subtle coherency regressions in rare long-context completions.
Samir: show me the command you used.
Mia: ```bash
python infra/eval/paired_eval.py \
  --model draft-13b-rogue-prefetch \
  --baseline draft-13b-std \
  --prompts data/stratified-5k.jsonl \
  --sampler two-tier --k1 4 --entropy-thresh 0.35 \
  --n 5000 --seed 42
```
Olivia: did you try quantized variant? many teams want to ship q4.
Mia: quickly: q4fmb on the same model + rogue-prefetch gave similar throughput gains vs q4 baseline but quality delta worsened (~1.2% win-rate drop). Seems quantization amplifies speculative bias.
Devin: that jives with our prior hypothesis — quant noise + premature KV use = hallucination risk.
Samir: can we tune entropy threshold per-quant profile? maybe tighten for q4.
Mia: tried thresholds 0.25..0.5 — q4 needed ~0.2 to match baseline win-rate but lost some speed. tradeoff zone.
Olivia: what's the ops risk? any downstream latency tail increase?
Mia: tails slightly wider for failed spec-fetch because we pay extra fallback penalty (additional model call). tail 95th latency +12ms on average, but overall p50 improved ~28ms.
Devin: for production we'd need adaptive fallback: if fallback rate > X% then route to safe model variant. can we surface fallback rate per route?
Samir: good call. add metrics: spec_hit_rate, fallback_rate, fallback_penalty_ms.
Mia: current quick results: spec_hit_rate=0.61, fallback_rate=0.39, fallback_penalty_ms=38.
Olivia: what about sampling stochasticity? did you lock RNG?
Mia: yes, seed=42 for paired runs. for stochastic samplers we used 10 Monte Carlo runs on 200 prompts to estimate variance — stddev on win-rate ~0.15%.
Devin: any clear failure modes? examples?
Mia: a few: long code completions where early tokens look ok but later function signature mismatches; multi-step logical chains sometimes diverged earlier. I pasted two short examples below.
Mia: Example 1 (dialog): 
Mia: "User: explain why X
Mia: Baseline: coherent 5-step answer
Mia: Prefetch: truncated explanation, invented an extra constraint in step 3"
Samir: can we add a conservative gating by token-position (don't prefetch for positions > 512)?
Mia: tried that — reduced regression count by ~30%, hit_rate fell to 0.48.
Olivia: what's the suggested eval to sign off? we need a reproducible commit for onboarding.
Devin: propose: 10k stratified prompts, paired human eval on 2k critical prompts, automated metrics (PPL, BLEU/ROUGE, pass@1 for code), and stability tests across quant levels (fp16, q4fmb, q8_0). baseline gating rules: max acceptable win-rate drop 0.5% and fallback_rate < 0.25.
Samir: add synthetic adversarial prompts (prompt-perturbations) to stress test speculative bias.
Mia: agreed. I'll run the full sweep with thresholds grid {0.15,0.2,0.25,0.3,0.35} across quant levels and collect: spec_hit_rate, fallback_rate, p50/p95 latency, win-rate, pplx.
Olivia: timeline?
Mia: starting EOD today, should have sweep summary in 48h.
Devin: also create an ops dashboard tile with fallback_rate and spec_hit_rate per model-route — tag the routes so we can auto-roll back if fallback_rate spikes.
Samir: I'll add a runbook snippet in ops-runbooks: if fallback_rate > 0.4 for >5min, revert to baseline.
ops-bot: note created: #incidents/rogue-prefetch-monitor with threshold=0.4, owner=Samir.
Mia: adding raw logs to /mnt/exp/rogue-prefetch/4387654321 — contains match pairs, examples, seeds.
Olivia: great — thanks. please attach the human eval rubric when you post the sweep results.
Mia: will do. ping me if you want early access to the sample diffs. :mag:
